summary: axe-core 4.13.0 (vendored) over every console page of the app's lane copy (the mold plus the app's packs), served on this machine by the lane world (molds/mold_v0/testing/console/: the lane copy's API on an embedded throwaway database behind the shell's own offline Clerk, one workspace owner who is also platform staff, `next start` on 127.0.0.1), with a row per pack and a row per page: the shell's own pages, each host pack's pages (its routes.json) and each pack's tabs, pages and record areas (the generated registry). A serious or critical WCAG 2.0/2.1/2.2 A or AA violation fails its page and its pack's row; so does an HTTP error, an error page, a signed-in page that sends its person to sign-in, or a page with no control to use: nothing measured is never a pass. Nothing deployed is contacted: the console and API listen on 127.0.0.1, start from an emptied environment, and every browser request or WebSocket a page opens off this machine is aborted and counted (service workers are blocked). The servers' own outbound fetches are kept off real services by that empty environment, not by a filter.

requires.else: Install the browser this lane drives: npm i -g playwright && npx playwright install chromium (and restore the vendored rule set from git: git checkout molds/mold_v0/testing/accessibility/vendor/axe.min.js).

checks.name: axe.console

requires.else: Install the product's own dependencies into the codebase's ignored folders (no lockfile is written there): npm --prefix molds/mold_v0/codebase ci && npm --prefix molds/mold_v0/codebase/orchestrator ci && npm --prefix molds/mold_v0/codebase/web install --no-package-lock

This lane copy has no scripts/lib/test-world.ts (the shell's throwaway world, with its offline Clerk in scripts/lib/mock-providers.ts), which the lane world is built on. The shell in molds/mold_v0/codebase must carry it; restore it from git (git checkout molds/mold_v0/codebase/scripts/lib) and run the lane again.
The console's dependencies are not installed, so its pages cannot be built here: npm --prefix molds/mold_v0/codebase/web install --no-package-lock

checks.why: A serious or critical WCAG violation is a person who cannot use the page at all: an unnamed button is invisible to a screen reader, failing contrast is unreadable in daylight. A row per pack shows which pack's pages carry it.

not_covered: The DEPLOYED console. These pages are the app's lane copy (build/<app_id>.lane/: the mold plus the app's packs, unbranded), built with `next build --webpack` and served by `next start` on 127.0.0.1 against the lane copy's own API on an embedded throwaway database: the same pages, components and styles the app ships, not the bytes Vercel or its server serves. The brand overlay (name, colour, logo) is graded by `branding.py check`, not here, so colour contrast is measured in the shell's own theme.

Clerk itself. A copy served on this machine cannot reach Clerk with the app's keys, so the console is built with a lane stand-in for `@clerk/nextjs` (molds/mold_v0/testing/console/clerk-standin/, in that build only) that reads the session the shell's own offline Clerk signs; the API verifies that session as it does in production. Clerk's sign-in and sign-up widgets (/auth/sign-in, /auth/sign-up), its user menu and organisation switcher popups are therefore not graded.

One identity and an empty workspace: the owner of one fresh workspace who is also platform staff. Pages are graded with no records, runs, keys or members (their empty states), and what a member, a viewer or a second workspace sees is not graded.
Dynamic pages with an identifier in the address (a record, an account, a docs article: /app/records/<area>/<key>, /admin/accounts/<slug>, /app/docs/<slug>) are not graded; their list pages are.
Keyboard-only traversal, focus order and visible focus: axe checks the accessibility tree and the rendered styles, not a person tabbing through the page.
Screen-reader output, zoom to 200%, reduced motion and forced colours.
Moderate and minor axe rules, and axe's `incomplete` results (a person must judge them): counted in the detail column, never failing.
A pack that adds no console page has no row of its own to grade; its row says `not-covered (adds no console page)`, never pass.
